subject.title: Guard Telegram and iMessage dispatch against fleet loops

question: Should Telegram/iMessage loop suppression live inside OpenClaw's channel-turn admission path, or may this PR rely on a host-local external `fleet-loop-guard` binary from shared dispatch?
rationale: This changes where OpenClaw enforces a channel safety boundary and whether inbound message/session data may be handed to untracked host code, which is a maintainer security and ownership decision rather than a routine patch detail.

options.title: Move into owned admission
options.body: Implement the guard in OpenClaw-owned channel or turn-kernel admission so suppression happens before session record and dispatch without an external executable.

options.title: Accept helper contract
options.body: Keep the helper only after maintainers explicitly define installation, versioning, timeout, data-sharing, and operator security expectations.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Close or pause this PR and track a narrower Telegram/iMessage loop design if the current fleet-only helper contract is not a product direction.

recommendation.title: Move into owned admission
recommendation.body: Implement the guard in OpenClaw-owned channel or turn-kernel admission so suppression happens before session record and dispatch without an external executable.

likelyOwner.reason: The generic bot-loop guard history and docs make this the closest existing owner boundary for deciding whether the PR should reuse that path or establish a new security contract.
